method: A one-shot PowerShell process sample (same technique as Processes.js's own loop), run through this worktree's PATCHED Processes.js — read-only, no server touched, no restart of the live Servex.

dev servers.note: 35 PROCESSES (cmd+conhost+node x2 per server tree), not 35 servers — see real_servers below

real_servers.how_counted: roots of the 'dev servers' process trees, minus the port-80 gate (gate.mjs is not a per-project server)

list.note: this task's own worktree, started by node Server/worktree-up.mjs; actively used right now, not idle

why_they_disagree: list_servers (Servex's own in-memory Process objects) and procs/*.json (the on-disk record Process.spawn_detached() writes) both only know about 'monorepo' — the one project whose Process instance persisted a restart-survival record. The 7 running worktree servers (qf-1..qf-6, dev-server-count) are real, live node run.js processes (confirmed by this sample) that Servex's own registry currently shows as status 'stopped': they most likely started under an EARLIER Servex process and survived a later Servex restart as parent-gone orphans, with no procs/<name>.json record of their own to be re-adopted from. The new process-table grouping is read-only and process-based, so it sees all 8; list_servers and procs/*.json are registry-based and currently under-count by 7. This is a pre-existing registry/reality gap in Worktrees/Process.js, not something this task's fix changes — logged for awareness, not fixed here (out of this brief's scope: deliverable 3 only asks about idle_enough()/stop_idle() skipping a worktree that SHOULD be stopped, and that gap is a separate, likely cause of such a skip if it ever happens — see idle_check below).

idle_check.what: For each running worktree server above, whether Worktrees.idle_enough() would call it idle right now.
idle_check.qf-1_through_qf-6: Never evaluated: stop_idle() skips every /^qf-\d+$/ name unconditionally (Worktrees.js:208) — these are quick-fix pool slots Pool.js manages on its own. Working as designed.
idle_check.dev-server-count: Not idle: this is the present task's own worktree, with a live agent (this session) working in it right now. idle_enough() would see its task un-paused, un-landed, with a live agent, and return null.
idle_check.finding: No idle (paused/landed/stopped) non-pool worktree currently holds a running server. page-index, refiner-step6 and runaway-search — three worktrees that WERE running earlier today per the brief's own 18:52 measurement — show status 'stopped' with no live process in this sample, i.e. stop_idle() already did its job for them. Nothing to fix on this pass (deliverable 3's 'fine outcome' case).

related_but_out_of_scope: The status desync above (list_servers/procs/*.json showing 1 real server where 8 run) means that IF a non-pool worktree server ever becomes a parent-gone orphan across a Servex restart while its task is idle, stop_idle()'s own check (`runner.status !== "stopped"`) would skip it, since the registry already (wrongly) says 'stopped' — so it would never be asked to stop, and would linger exactly as the owner's ask worried. No such case was found live today, so no fix was made; worth a line in Worktrees.js's own doc/processes.md as a known gap for whoever next touches Process.js's restart-survival records.
